abstract: Bloomberry (powered by Revealera) analyzed 180 million global job postings from company websites spanning January 2023 to October 2025 to identify which jobs AI is actually replacing in the labor market. The analysis used a supervised learning pipeline with 650 normalized job titles developed via Amazon Mechanical Turk labeling, a fine-tuned Sentence Transformer using contrastive learning, and a Random Forest classifier for multi-class prediction. Against an overall market decline of 8% in 2025 vs. 2024, creative execution roles showed dramatically steeper declines: computer graphic artist postings fell 33%, photographers and writers each dropped 28%, and journalists/reporters declined 22%. Regulatory and environmental roles also contracted sharply (corporate compliance specialists -29%, sustainability specialists -28%). Notably, creative leadership roles (directors, managers, producers) showed significantly more resilience than execution-focused positions. On the growth side, machine learning engineer postings surged 40%, robotics engineers grew 11%, and data center engineers rose 9%. Software engineering roles remained largely stable despite AI coding tool proliferation, and data analyst/management positions slightly outperformed the market.
keyFindings: Computer graphic artist postings fell 33% in 2025, photographers and writers each fell 28%, and journalists/reporters declined 22%, all substantially exceeding the 8% overall market decline.

Creative leadership roles (directors, managers, producers) were significantly more resilient than execution-focused positions, suggesting AI displaces production tasks more than strategic/managerial ones.
Machine learning engineer postings surged 40%, the largest increase of any category, while robotics engineers (+11%) and data center engineers (+9%) also grew.
Software engineering roles remained largely stable despite widespread AI coding tool adoption, contradicting displacement fears for developers.
Senior leadership postings declined only 1.7% (outperforming the market by 6.3pp), while individual contributor roles fell 9%, reinforcing a seniority gradient in AI resilience.
methodology: Analysis of 180 million global job postings from company websites (January 2023-October 2025) via Revealera's jobs data platform. Job title normalization used a taxonomy of 650 titles developed through human labeling on Amazon Mechanical Turk. Classification pipeline: fine-tuned Sentence Transformer with contrastive learning generated dense vector embeddings from job descriptions, then a Random Forest classifier performed multi-class job title prediction across all 180M postings. Year-over-year percentage changes calculated between 2024 and 2025.
qualifiers: Job posting volume does not directly equate to employment levels — postings reflect employer demand signals, which can be influenced by hiring freezes, consolidation of roles, or shifts to internal mobility. The 8% overall decline in postings may reflect macroeconomic factors beyond AI. The analysis cannot distinguish between AI-driven and non-AI-driven causes of decline. Geographic and industry breakdowns are limited. The ML classification pipeline introduces some misclassification noise across 650 categories. Revealera is a relatively new data provider whose coverage and sampling methodology have not been independently validated.
